role.altitude: The room service server keeps delivering, presenting the check and dealing with the guest at the door; printing checks, keying room charges and carrying signed slips to the front office shrink.
skills_to_grow: Closing checks on the handheld at the door
role.ambitious_version: A server whose charges are on the guest's bill before the lift doors close.

tasks.short: Have the room service order rung in, collect the totaled check, present it to the guest, accept payment or a room-charge signature, key the charge to the guest's bill and hand in the signed checks.

steps.what: Order taker rings the room service order into the till
Server totals the check in the till and prints it for the tray
Server presents the check to the guest at the room and gets the room-charge signature
Server accepts card or cash payment from guests who do not charge to the room
Server checks the check on the handheld before closing it: room number, guest name, items and the signed amount
Server posts the room charge to the guest's bill: keys the room number and closes the check in the till at the station today; after the change closes it on the handheld at the door
Server hands the signed checks to the front office for the night audit

approvals.approved_version: The room charge with room number, guest name, items and the amount the guest signed exactly as checked by the server in s5c, posted once to that guest's bill in the property system; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: The check prints automatically with the kitchen ticket once the order taker rings the order into the till ({OTHER}), so the server only picks it up. At the door the guest signs on the server's handheld, and after the server checks room number, items and signed amount, closing the check there posts the room charge once to the guest's bill through the till's link to the hotel's property system; card payments are taken on the same handheld. Signed checks are stored with the transaction, so only the few paper slips go to the front office. Presenting the check and dealing with the guest stay with the server.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charges were keyed at the station after each delivery and signed slips carried to the front office.
tasks.enabler_now: Hotel tills link to property systems and run on handhelds with signature capture.
tasks.still_hard: Guests who query a charge at the door.
tasks.human_edge: Handling a disputed bill politely at a guest's door.
tasks.altitude: Less station time between deliveries; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Reconcile outlet charges with guest bills
reach.learn: Whether direct room charges cut late postings.

evidence.claim: Hotel tills post room charges to the property system and capture signatures on handhelds.
The tax office advises a reliable till system and seven years' retention of records.
Per-server sales logs can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the order in the till to checks handed in; night audit is outside.
Input contract for s2: the order rung into the till by the order taker in s1, as today; the check prints with the kitchen ticket.
Input contract for s5: the server's close action and the guest's signature on the handheld at the door; the till's link to the property system, set up by the hotel's IT, posts the charge.
Coverage: a handheld goes with about 80% of deliveries; the rest are keyed at the station and handed in on paper; s5 and s6 are priced at that share.
Presenting the check and payments keep their full time; the order taker's time is outside the server's savings.

The check before posting keeps its full time. s2 keeps 30 for picking up the printed check and the odd reprint; s5 keeps 30 for the deliveries without a handheld and the close action; s6 keeps 20 for the paper slips.
unknowns: Whether the hotel's till links to its property system.
research_questions: Do late room charges fall at check-out?

already_counted.description: Server fixes room charges the property system rejects.

incremental.description: Server charges and logs in the handheld each shift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a handheld goes with only half of deliveries, at night none, so s5 and s6 keep 60 (24.0); high: a handheld goes with about 80% of deliveries as assumed (34.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
